context_prompt: The industrial asset class is hydroelectric power turbine
ds_context: The failure modes of a hydroelectric power turbine include cracks or fractures in the turbine blades, bending or twisting of the turbine shaft, wear or failure of the bearings, leaks in the seals, malfunction or failure of the hydro-mechanical governors, malfunction or failure of the control systems, and overheating or failure of the generator. These failures can be caused by fatigue due to cyclic loading, overloading or excessive loading, corrosion due to moisture or chemical attack, wear and tear due to friction or erosion, manufacturing defects, insufficient lubrication, or inadequate maintenance or inspection. The severity of these failures can range from low to high, with high severity failures leading to critical failures and system shutdown. The ability to detect these failures can vary, with some failures being easily detectable through regular inspection and maintenance, while others may be difficult to detect until failure occurs. Preventive maintenance measures include regular inspection and maintenance of the turbine blades, shaft, bearings, seals, governors, control systems, and generators, lubrication management to prevent wear and corrosion, monitoring of vibration, temperature, and other operating parameters to detect degradation, and implementation of redundancy and protection systems to minimize the impact of failures. It is important to conduct a detailed FMEA for each specific application to ensure accurate and effective risk assessment and management.
